item.title: AI Engineering Fundamentals: From Models to Products
item.description:
Simple definition#

AI engineering is the discipline of building applications on top of foundation models that someone else has usually trained. Instead of collecting data and training a model first, you start from a model that already works, then adapt it — with prompts, context, tools, fine-tuning — and wrap it in the product, evaluation and operations it needs.

item.title: From Generative to Agentic AI: Five Levels, SPAR and the Three Keystones
item.description:
Simple definition#

Generative AI produces content when asked. Agentic AI pursues a goal: it plans, uses tools, takes actions across systems, remembers, and improves from results — with as little human prompting as the task allows.

item.title: Agentic AI Strategy and Operating Model
item.description:
Simple definition#

An agentic AI strategy decides where agents should do work in the organisation, how much autonomy they get, what platform they run on, how value and risk are measured, and how people and processes change around them. It turns isolated pilots into a governed, scalable capability.

item.title: A Practical Playbook for Building AI Agents: Opportunity Scoring and the A.G.E.N.T. Framework
item.description:
Simple definition#

This playbook covers the practical path from “we should use agents” to an agent that works in production: find the right opportunity, score and prioritise it, design the agent with a structured framework, and implement it with principles that avoid the most common failures.

item.title: GenAI Adoption Strategy for the Enterprise
item.description:
Simple definition#

A GenAI adoption strategy decides where generative AI should create value, which capabilities the organisation buys or builds, which models and deployments it standardises on, how risk is governed, and how people and processes change — so that AI moves from scattered experiments to a measured, repeatable capability.

item.title: Hybrid AI in Financial Services: Practical Decisions
item.description:
Simple definition#

In financial services, hybrid AI means running each AI workload in the place its data, regulation and economics allow: frontier models through in-region cloud for tasks that need the best reasoning, open-weight or licensed models on the bank’s own infrastructure for restricted data and high-volume work, and one governed control plane across both.
